doc.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: The Beauty video, the lick and the tune Dorm Life
summary: The trio's lick was rehearsed, a tune written in college called Dorm Life, retitled When It Comes to regain publishing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There’s a tune or a video on your website, I believe it was “Beauty” it came from that. And the trio is in a club and I don’t know what the tune was but near the end you guys started playing. I think you started this thing. And the rhythm was like [scats]. And the first time you played it the other guys were not playing it with you. And the second time they started playing with you. And by the third time or so it became this thing and when people got to the end of the lick everybody stopped and there was this glorious silence. And you did it a few times, and then you ended. And I don’t have a question here except that it was really effective and I guess I wondered did that happen on the fly?

If it’s what I think you’re talking about, no. I mean it could have been called on on the fly, but it’s a part of a conversation that the people in the band were used to having. I don’t know if you remember this little skit on “Sesame Street” and it would say [scats]. That’s really, if you know “Manamana” then you know to go [scats]. It’s a tune of mine that if everyone knows, we play it together. And it’s interesting because everybody, you know, sometimes the drummer may not know it and the bass player knows it so you end up playing, and, “Oh okay, got it.” You know but it’s a tune I wrote in college. It’s called “Dorm Life” it’s just a blues. But it’s another title on a few other records called “When It Comes” and basically that’s the reason — the business reason — the first version of the song was on a record label that took the artist’s publishing. So when I did it on another song I re-named it. You’ll see that a lot on certain artists where you’re like well why does it have two titles? Because you’re trying to get your song back. Yep.
